newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RYNE SANDBERG TO RETIRE AGAIN AT END OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RYNE SANDBERG TO RETIRE AGAIN AT END OF SEASON.

text.p: Hall of Fame bound second baseman Ryne Sandberg Saturday announced that he will retire for the second time at the end of the season, his 15th with the Chicago Cubs.

The 37-year-old Sandberg, who walked away from the game in the middle of the 1994 season but returned for the 1996 campaign, was batting .249 this year with six homers and 40 RBI entering Saturday's game against the Dodgers.
After making his announcement, Sandberg hit two homers -- his seventh and eighth -- to lead Chicago to a 5-1 victory.

The 10-time All-Star is the only second baseman in major league history to win nine Gold Glove awards and boasts a better fielding percentage and more home runs than any second baseman in baseball history.
After sitting out a year and a half, the popular Sandberg came back to the Cubs and hit .244 with 25 home runs and 92 RBI last season.

Sandberg won the 1984 Most Valuable Player Award when he batted a career-high .314 with 19 home runs and 84 RBI in leading the Cubs to the National League East title. He became the first Cub to be named MVP since Ernie Banks in 1959.

"Everybody has their time, and my time has come," Sandberg said at a Wrigley Field news conference. "I've enjoyed myself here. I've grown up in Chicago and I think it's perfect that I'm retiring as a Cub."
Sandberg has 278 career homers, a .284 batting average, 341 stolen bases, 1,037 RBI and 2,350 hits in 2,125 games.

Sandberg had career highs with 40 home runs and 100 RBI in 1990 and also knocked in 100 runs in 1991. He was the first second baseman to lead the National League in homers since Rogers Hornsby hit 39 in 1925.
